The successful use of itraconazole has been re- ported in a few patients1-4 with cutaneous disease but infections with Leishmania aethiopica may not respond.5 Although a pilot study6 in patients with mucocutaneous leishmaniasis reported benefit with itraconazole this was not confirmed in another study7 where the response was only transient in the majority of patients. Similarly, itraconazole with terbinafine has been found to be ineffective in post kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis.8 1. Albanese G, et al. Cutaneous leishmaniasis: treatment with itra- conazole.
